NEW DELHI: The Election Commission has rejected reports of differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), saying all decisions related to the exercise were taken "unanimously".The poll body clarified that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi did raise concerns over some aspects of voter roll deletion and database handling, but these did not amount to disagreement with the final decisions taken by the Commission.The clarification came after an Indian Express report triggered a row by claiming that the two Election Commissioners had raised objections to the Commission's decisions 14 times over the past 10 months during the SIR exercise.EC sources told PTI that all decisions taken by the Election Commission, including those related to the SIR, were unanimous and had the approval of Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi as well as Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Responding to queries, officials said Sandhu and Joshi had flagged issues related to the deletion of names from electoral rolls in various states and the handling of voter data.Officials also pointed out that the law governing the Election Commission, as well as a Supreme Court judgment, provides that decisions should, as far as possible, be taken unanimously. Where unanimity is not possible, the majority view prevails.Meanwhile, opposition sharpened its attack on the Election Commission over the SIR, claiming it was meant to target electors not aligned to the BJP and its allies.Urging the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognizance of the issue, several opposition parties attacked Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and accused him of becoming a puppet of those in power.In a social media post, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav accused the poll panel of hatching a conspiracy to "wipe out democracy.""This is an extremely serious news that in the past 10 months, 2 Election Commissioners have registered their objections 14 times against the Election Commission's wrong decisions," Akhilesh said."This directly means that all Election Commissioners are not able to perform their rightful duties. If the members of an independent body do not have the freedom to carry out just actions or if there is no hearing of theirs, then these are extremely fatal and dangerous circumstances for democracy. For some people to betray democracy by becoming puppets of those in power is a grave constitutional crime. This is nothing less than a conspiracy to wipe out democracy," he added.Mamata Trinamool Congress (MTMC) also slammed CEC Kumar and said that the opposition should reintroduce the impeachment motion against Kumar in Parliament."Five months ago, more than 60 Rajya Sabha Members of Parliament... when only 50 were needed, wrote to the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha moving a motion to remove the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, that was five months ago. Now today, after this big news break that two Election Commissioners objected to many of the CEC's actions, it's time to bring out the Rajya Sabha motion to impeach the CEC and save democracy," MTMC's Derek O' O'Brien said.The issue is likely to escalate further as leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been vehement in his criticism of the Election Commission and the SIR process, alleging that it has resulted in the denial of voting rights.
Article Summary: The Election Commission has rejected reports of differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) The poll body clarified that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi did raise concerns over some aspects of voter roll deletion and database handling.

Article Title: Rajya Sabha polls for 12 seats: BJP likely to retain 8 in UP, SP eyes gain, BSP at risk
Article Text:
BJP likely to retain 8 UP seats, SP eyes 2, BSP faces exit

NEW DELHI: The BJP is set to have the numbers on its side in the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh, with the party-led alliance expected to win eight of the 10 seats going to polls in the state. The Samajwadi Party could take the remaining two seats, based on the current strength of parties in the assembly.The Election Commission on Tuesday announced polls for 12 Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal. Voting, if required, will be held on October 16, with the results also to be declared the same day.The BJP is also expected to add one seat to its Rajya Sabha tally by winning the lone seat from West Bengal. The seat became vacant after actor Rukmini Mallick, popularly known as Koel, resigned from the House. The Trinamool Congress had sent her to the Rajya Sabha before losing power in the assembly election held earlier this year.In Uttar Pradesh, the BJP-led alliance has around 290 MLAs, while the SP-Congress combine has about 103. A candidate needs around 37 votes to win a Rajya Sabha seat.The BJP can comfortably win seven seats, while the SP-Congress combine can secure two.The contest for the 10th seat could be closer, with the BJP-led alliance starting with around 31 votes against around 29 for the SP-Congress side.The polls could also mark the end of the BSP's representation in Parliament. Mayawati's party has no member in the Lok Sabha and its only MLA in Uttar Pradesh, Uma Shankar Singh, died in August. The term of BSP's lone Rajya Sabha member, Ramji Gautam, ends in November.Gautam is among the nine Uttar Pradesh members whose terms are ending. The others are Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri, BJP leaders Arun Singh, Geeta Shakya, Neeraj Shekhar, Brijlal, B L Verma and Seema Dwivedi, and SP leader Ram Gopal Yadav.Puri's continuation in the Union Cabinet will depend on whether the BJP nominates him for another Rajya Sabha term.The 10th Uttar Pradesh seat was held by former deputy chief minister Dinesh Sharma. It became vacant earlier this month after Sharma resigned from the Rajya Sabha following his appointment as lieutenant governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.The BSP had managed to retain its Rajya Sabha presence in 2020 after the BJP fielded only eight candidates for 10 seats. The move allowed the BSP and SP to each elect one member unopposed.Gautam was elected unopposed after the nomination of an SP-backed Independent candidate was rejected. The SP had then alleged an understanding between the BJP and BSP.In Uttarakhand, BJP Rajya Sabha member Naresh Bansal's term is ending. The BJP, which has a comfortable majority in the state assembly, is expected to retain the seat.The election notification will be issued on September 29. Candidates can file nominations till October 6. Polling and counting will take place on October 16, if required.
Article Summary: BJP likely to retain 8 UP seats, SP eyes 2, BSP faces exit. Election Commission on Tuesday announced polls for 12 Rajya Sabha seats. Voting, if required, will be held on October 16, with results also to be declared the same day.

Article Title: ED appeal ‘abuse of process’ in National Herald case: Gandhis

NEW DELHI: Congress netas Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi have said it is “abuse of the process of law” that ED has challenged in Delhi high court a trial court order refusing to take cognisance of its chargesheet against them in the National Herald-linked money laundering case.In a response filed in the high court, the Gandhis opposed ED’s revision plea saying it is “not maintainable” as trial court’s order is “perfectly legal and sound in law and does not suffer from any jurisdictional error, perversity, irregularity or illegality”.On Tuesday, Justice Sachin Datta was informed by the Gandhis’ counsel that they had filed their replies on Sept 18. HC has listed the matter for Oct 12.“Petitioner (ED) has miserably failed to demonstrate that the complaint filed by ED was maintainable under statutory provisions applicable to case. It is writ large that the words ‘private complaint’ or ‘a complaint by a public person/citizen’ do not find place in the statutory framework,” they contended.On Dec 16, 2025, trial court had held that cognisance of the agency’s complaint in the case was “impermissible in law” as it was not founded on an FIR.In its order, trial court had said ED’s probe stemmed from a private complaint, and not an FIR. Despite receiving the complaint made by BJP neta Subramanian Swamy and the consequent summoning order in 2014, CBI refrained from registering an FIR in relation to the alleged scheduled offence.ED claimed that trial court order has, in effect, given a hall pass to a category of money launderers only on ground that scheduled offence is reported by a private individual by way of a complaint to a magistrate.Opposing ED’s plea, Gandhis said this case provides the only instance where a non-statutory complaint by a private person has been made the foundation for initiating proceedings under the PMLA.
Article Summary: Congress netas Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi have said it is “abuse of the process of law’ ED has challenged in Delhi high court a trial court order refusing to take cognisance of its chargesheet against them in the National Herald-linked money laundering case. NEW DELHI: Giving a twist to the five-year-old Lakhimpur Kheri case in which Asish Mishra, the son of former Union minister Ajay Mishra, is accused of mowing down four protesting farmers with his vehicle, advocate Prashant Bhushan Tuesday accused the trial judge of attempting to intimidate witnesses and derail the trial.Bhushan told a SC bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that when a prime witness had sought deferment of his deposition on medical grounds, the trial judge issued non-bailable arrest warrants against him.“The judicial officer needs to be changed. Otherwise, there will be a complete miscarriage of justice, I can guarantee that,” Bhushan said.He said the judge was causing havoc in the district as he took NDPS and SC/ST Act cases for himself and acquitted the accused.The bench said it was more worrying that the public prosecutor had been giving up on testimonies of vital witnesses. The court asked UP govt to ensure that the present public prosecutor was replaced with a seasoned one or the most senior in the district. It also told the state to instruct the new public prosecutor to recall witnesses who had been given up by the prosecution to depose before the trial court.Referring to allegations of a large number of acquittals rendered by the trial judge in serious cases, the bench asked the SC registry to forward Bhushan’s complaint to the Allahabad HC Chief Justice and requested him to take necessary action. It asked the HC registry to file an action taken report before SC.Last Oct, court had asked UP police to examine allegations of attempts by Mishra to influence witnesses. Mishra is out on bail but has been barred from residing in Lakhimpur Kheri, his hometown.

Article Title: 'Non-application of mind': Court sets aside order refusing probe in Sonia Gandhi electoral roll case
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Monday allowed a revision plea challenging a magistrate's order refusing to probe the allegation that Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's name was included in the electoral roll in 1980, three years before she acquired Indian citizenship.Special Judge Vishal Gogne delivered the judgment two days after deferring it. He quashed the order as "non-speaking" or an order that does not explain the reasons behind a judge's conclusion."The impugned order suffers from a manifest error in law on account of non-compliance with Section 175(3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), inter alia, not hearing the submissions of the police officer concerned and non-calling of a status report from the police station concerned," the Special Judge noted."The 'non-speaking' nature of the order was evident as the magistrate did not consider the twin options under law of directing the registration of an FIR or alternatively conducting proceedings under the BNSS, and instead of considering the core aspect of whether the complaint disclosed the commission of a cognisable offence, the magistrate digressed towards the issue of citizenship," he added.The court remanded the matter back to the magistrate to pass a reasoned order after hearing fresh arguments.The matter has been posted for further proceedings on September 29.In September last year, advocate Vikas Tripathi filed a plea in a Delhi magistrate's court seeking action against Sonia Gandhi, claiming her name appeared on the electoral rolls three years before she became an Indian citizen in 1983. The plea had sought a police investigation into what it terms a possible case of forgery.The application had pointed to documents suggesting Sonia Gandhi took Indian citizenship on April 30, 1983. Yet, her name allegedly appeared as a voter in the New Delhi constituency roll in 1980, was deleted in 1982, and re-entered in April 1983 after she formally became an Indian national.Tripathi's plea was dismissed on September 11, 2025, prompting him to approach a higher court.
Article Summary: A Delhi court allowed a revision plea challenging a magistrate's order refusing to probe the allegation that Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's name was included in the electoral roll in 1980. Special Judge Vishal Gogne quashed the order as "non-speaking" or an order that does not explain the reasons behind a judge's conclusion.

Article Title: Kejriwal, Sisodia, Sanjay Singh get 4 weeks to reply in Delhi HC contempt case
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court on Monday listed for hearing on November 16 a criminal contempt case against AAP leaders Arvind Kejriwal, Manish Sisodia, Sanjay Singh and others over allegedly “vilifying” social media posts targeting Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma.A bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Arun Bhardwaj granted Kejriwal and the other accused four weeks to file their replies.Kejriwal’s senior counsel told the court that he was yet to receive the complete material on the basis of which the contempt proceedings were initiated. The bench directed the registry to provide the material, which was stated to be incomplete.“Reply, if any, to be filed in four weeks,” the bench said.The court also listed for November 16 a separate contempt petition filed by lawyer Ashok Chaitanya against Kejriwal and others, including AAP leader Gopal Rai and journalist Saurav Das. The petition alleges that they were part of an “orchestrated social media campaign” against Justice Sharma.Justice Sharma had initiated criminal contempt proceedings on May 14 against Kejriwal, Sisodia, Singh and other AAP leaders, including Durgesh Pathak, Saurabh Bharadwaj and Vinay Mishra, over allegedly “vilifying” social media posts concerning her handling of the Delhi excise policy case.Contempt proceedings were also initiated against X user Devesh Vishwakarma.It was further noted the circulation of clips from court proceedings and said the proposed contemnors were attempting to create a “parallel narrative”. She observed that “remaining silent” in such circumstances would not amount to judicial restraint but a “surrender before a powerful litigant”.The contempt proceedings stem from the excise policy case. On February 27, a trial court discharged Kejriwal, Sisodia and 21 others, holding that the prosecution’s case could not withstand judicial scrutiny.
Article Summary: The Delhi High Court will hear a criminal contempt case against AAP leaders on November 16. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma had initiated criminal contempt proceedings on May 14 against Kejriwal, Sisodia, Singh and other AAP leaders. The court also listed for November 16 a separate contempt petition filed by lawyer Ashok Chaitanya.

Article Title: 'Method of disenfranchising Indians': Kharge slams SIR, calls it a 'Frankenstein monster'
Article Text:
Congress leader Mallikarjun Kharge has lambasted the Election Commission's electoral roll revision, labeling it a misguided 'Frankenstein Monster' that adversely affects its constituents

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Monday stepped up his attack on the Election Commission ’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, describing the exercise as a “Frankenstein Monster” after several prominent political and government figures were issued notices in Delhi.“What started as SIR from Bihar has now knocked on Delhi’s door, and perhaps now the powers-that-be are realizing why the Congress Party has been calling the entire process flawed from day one!” Kharge said in a post on X.“SIR is not just a tool used by the BJP for vote theft and dismantling democracy, it’s a flawed process that has turned into a Frankenstein Monster, now trapping its own people!!”Kharge referred to notices issued to BJP veteran Lal Krishna Advani, external affairs minister S Jaishankar, former vice-president Jagdeep Dhankhar, Delhi Lieutenant Governor, Rajya Sabha members, former Union ministers and other prominent figures. He also referred to an earlier controversy involving Bharat Ratna-winning scientist C N R Rao and former Navy chief Admiral Arun Prakash.The Congress president also questioned the Election Commission’s reference to “VIP/marked electors”, linking it to the constitutional principle of equal voting rights.“Is there now some Special Category of voters in India’s Universal Adult Franchise, VIP voters and ordinary voters?” Kharge asked. “Isn’t this a violation of the constitutional principle of One Person, One Vote, One Value? Has the VIP vote become more valuable now?”Kharge also cited the situation in West Bengal, where Election Commission data submitted before the Supreme Court showed that 1,26,194 appeals against exclusion had been decided.Of these, 1,13,943 voters were ordered to be restored to the electoral rolls, while 8,649 appeals were rejected. Kharge highlighted the fact that around 93 percent of the decided appeals had resulted in restoration.The figure, however, relates only to appeals decided so far and does not mean that 93 percent of all excluded voters were found to have been wrongly removed. More than 37 lakh appeals remained pending, according to the Election Commission data.SIR is an intensive revision of electoral rolls in which election officials verify existing electors and identify entries requiring correction, deletion or further verification. The exercise was first conducted in Bihar before being expanded to other states and Union territories. The process has faced political opposition and legal scrutiny over the verification criteria, documents required and safeguards available to voters.In Delhi, the draft electoral roll published on August 31 contained around 97.5 lakh electors. Around 33.13 lakh voters were identified for notices after their records could not be mapped to the previous intensive revision or were flagged for what officials described as logical discrepancies. More than 31.63 lakh notices had been served as of Sunday.Among those flagged were Advani, Jaishankar, Dhankhar, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, AAP leader Arvind Kejriwal, former deputy chief minister Manish Sisodia and several senior officials. Some cases have already been cleared after documents were verified.The Delhi CEO has maintained that receiving an SIR notice does not mean deletion from the electoral roll. The notices form part of the verification process, and voters are allowed to submit documents and make representations before any decision is taken. The final electoral roll is scheduled to be published on November 4.
Article Summary: Congress leader Mallikarjun Kharge has lambasted the Election Commission's electoral roll revision. He described the exercise as a misguided 'Frankenstein Monster' that adversely affects its constituents. Kharge referred to notices issued to BJP veteran Lal Krishna Advani, external affairs minister S Jaishankar, former vice-president Jagdeep Dhankhar.

Article Text: New Delhi: Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi have said it is “abuse of the process of law” that ED has challenged in Delhi High Court a trial court order refusing to take cognisance of its charge sheet against them in the National Herald-linked money laundering case.In a response filed in HC, the Gandhis have opposed ED’s revision petition, saying it is “not maintainable” as the trial court’s order is “perfectly legal and sound in law and does not suffer from any jurisdictional error, perversity, irregularity or illegality”.Tuesday, Justice Sachin Datta was informed by the Gandhis’ counsel that they filed the replies on Sept 18. The court listed the matter for further hearing on Oct 12.“The petitioner (ED) has miserably failed to demonstrate that the complaint filed by the ED was maintainable on the basis of the statutory provisions, applicable to the case. It is writ large that the words ‘private complaint’ or ‘a complaint by a public person/citizen’, do not find any place in the entire statutory framework,” they contended.On Dec 16, 2025, the trial court had held that cognisance of the agency’s complaint in the case was “impermissible in law” as it was not founded on an FIR.In its order, the trial court had said that the agency’s probe stemmed from a private complaint, and not an FIR, and despite receiving the complaint made by BJP leader Subramanian Swamy and the consequent summoning order in 2014, the CBI refrained from registering an FIR in relation to the alleged scheduled offence.ED, in its plea in the high court, claimed that the trial court order has in effect given a hall pass to a category of money launderers only on the ground that the scheduled offence is reported by a private individual by way of a complaint to a magistrate.Opposing ED’s plea, the Gandhis said this case provides the only instance where a non-statutory complaint by a private person has been made the foundation of initiating proceedings under the PMLA.The reply also mentioned that ED has filed the petition in the high court at “lightning speed” as the order was passed by the trial court on Dec 16, 2025, and the agency approached the high court on Dec 17.
Article Summary: ED has challenged a trial court order refusing to take cognisance of its charge sheet against them in the National Herald-linked money laundering case. In a response filed in HC, the Gandhis have opposed ED’s revision petition, saying it is “not maintainable’

Article Title: DTC Bus Hits Scooter, 19-Year-Old Dies; Driver Arrested
Article Text: New Delhi: A 19-year-old man died after his scooter was hit by a DTC bus on the Najafgarh–Nangloi Road Tuesday. The driver of the bus was subsequently arrested.The victim was taken to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital in Mangol Puri, where doctors declared him dead.Police found the DTC bus driver, Amit Dahiya, at the spot of the accident and took him to the police station. During enquiry, police found another injured person, Monu Kumar , who had been admitted to Rathi Hospital. But Monu was later declared unfit to provide a statement.The deceased was identified as Himanshu (19), a resident of Bahadurgarh. His body has been preserved in the hospital mortuary for a post-mortem.A case has been registered under sections relating to rash driving on a public way, act endangering life or personal safety of others and causing death by negligence under BNS. Further investigation is in progress.
Article Summary: A 19-year-old man died after his scooter was hit by a DTC bus on the Najafgarh–Nangloi Road. The driver of the bus was subsequently arrested. The victim was taken to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital in Mangol Puri, where doctors declared him dead.

Article Title: Mahayuti allies spar over two seats in Pune division as MLC polls for graduates and teachers' constituencies announced
Article Text:
The voting will be held on Oct 23, with counting and results on Oct 27

Kolhapur:





Political activity in Pune division has gathered momentum with Election Commission on Tuesday announcing biennial elections to Maharashtra Legislative Council from graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies. The voting will be held on Oct 23, with counting and results on Oct 27.The Pune division constituency — covering Pune, Satara, Solapur, Sangli, and Kolhapur districts — will elect one representative each from the graduates and teachers’ constituencies to the legislative council. Even before the formal election process began, political activity in Pune division had intensified, particularly within Mahayuti, where BJP Shiv Sena and NCP have staked a claim to the two seats.BJP has asserted its traditional hold over both the constituencies, pointing out that it won the seats repeatedly in the past. Senior BJP member and minister Chandrakant Patil, a two-time MLC from the graduates’ constituency, has already begun projecting Vivekanand College chief executive officer Kaustubh Gawade as a likely face for the teachers’ constituency and Kranti Sugar Factory chairperson Sharad Lad for the graduates’ constituency at public gatherings.Alliance partner Shiv Sena has also thrown its hat into the ring by declaring deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde’s close aide Mangesh Chivate as its aspirant for the teachers’ constituency. The party has also floated Eknath Swabhimani Shikshak Sanghatana and stepped up outreach efforts through meetings and gatherings of teachers across the division.NCP, meanwhile, has staked a claim to the graduates’ seat, citing its victory in the last election. The constituency is currently represented by Arun Lad of NCP. State minister Hasan Mushrif is backing his close associate Pratap alias Bhaiya Mane for the seat. Mushrif has publicly claimed that Arun had persuaded Mane to withdraw from the previous contest by assuring him of support in the subsequent election. He has now challenged Arun to ensure that his son Sharad, whom Mushrif alleges has moved closer to BJP, does not seek the party nomination.The graduates’ constituency is emerging as a crowded field. Former MLC Ranjeetsinha Mohite-Patil of Akluj in Solapur district has also begun preparations for the contest. A key meeting of his supporters has been convened on Sept 24.In Pune division, Arun Lad of NCP won the graduates’ constituency in the previous election, while Congress candidate Jayant Asgaonkar emerged victorious from the teachers’ constituency.Unlike in assembly and Lok Sabha elections, voters in MLC graduates and teachers’ constituencies must register afresh for every election. As voting is conducted through the preferential voting system, aspiring candidates and political parties have already launched intensive enrolment drives to maximise the number of eligible voters before the nomination process concludes.
Article Summary: Election Commission announces biennial elections to Maharashtra Legislative Council from graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies. The voting will be held on Oct 23, with counting and results on Oct 27. The Pune division constituency — covering Pune, Satara, Solapur, Sangli, and Kolhapur districts — will elect one representative each to the legislative council.

Article Title: 46-yr-old woman dies after come under dumper truck
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





A 46-year-old woman, a resident of Kanan Nagar, died after being run over by a dumper truck after she slipped while riding a two-wheeler.The deceased was identified as Punam Rameshwar Shinde. Punam was driving the vehicle while her daughter was riding pillion. The mother-daughter duo were heading home from Dabholkar Corner.At Bakers’ Lane, Punam tried to overtake, but her vehicle went into rough sand and slipped. She fell down and came under the rear wheels of the dumper truck that was coming from behind.Punam was rushed to CPR hospital, where she was declared dead. Shahupuri police registered a case of accidental death.“We have detained the truck driver. The family members carried out the funeral and are grieving. Once we get a complaint, we will proceed with registering the crime and further investigation,” inspector Santosh Doke from Shahupuri police station said.
Article Summary: A 46-year-old woman, a resident of Kanan Nagar, died after being run over by a dumper truck. Punam Rameshwar Shinde was driving the vehicle while her daughter was riding pillion. The mother-daughter duo were heading home from Dabholkar Corner.

Article Title: Cops on Ganpati patrol hit by speeding MUV on Thane-Belapur Road, driver flees
Article Text:
The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday.





NAVI MUMBAI: In a hit-and-run incident on the Thane-Belapur Road, a police constable and a woman assistant sub-inspector (ASI) were injured when a speeding MUV rammed into their motorcycle from behind while they were patrolling during the seventh day of Ganpati immersion.The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday.The injured cops were identified as constable Umesh Patil, 41, who was riding his personal motorcycle, and ASI Rashmin Magar, who was riding pillion.The motorcycle skidded after being hit by the MUV. Patil sustained injuries to his left leg, while Magar suffered bruises to her left elbow, shoulder and left leg.Acting on a complaint filed by Patil, Rabale MIDC police registered an FIR under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Motor Vehicles Act against the MUV driver. Police traced him to his residence in Ghansoli.Devidas Kathale, senior inspector of Rabale MIDC police, said, “As the accused MUV driver's wife is due to deliver in a few days, he will be summoned to the police station later and served with a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.”
Article Summary: The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday. The injured cops were identified as constable Umesh Patil, 41, and ASI Rashmin Magar, who was riding pillion. The motorcycle skidded after being hit by the MUV.

Article Title: Speeding SUV hits bike in Vashi, 3 youths injured; driver traced
Article Text:
Accused driver of SUV Mahindra Thar escaping after accident





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday.The incident took place around 1am. The injured youths were initially taken to NMMC Hospital in Vashi and were later referred to Sion Hospital for further treatment.Following the incident, a biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police then traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number.During the investigation, it was learnt that the owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride. Police subsequently traced his mobile tower location to an area near the creek in Sector 12, Vashi, where he was allegedly hiding.He was detained and served a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), following which he was released.
Article Summary: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday. A biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number. The owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride.

Article Title: Quack doctor detained in Maharashtra for practising medicine without registration
Article Text:
A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel police after an inspection (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel taluka police after a complaint was lodged by the medical officer of the Primary Health Centre at Ajivali village in Panvel taluka, following an inspection by health department officials at his illegal clinic in Kasalkhand village on Monday afternoon.The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal and resides in an MHADA building in India Bulls Township, Kon village, Panvel.Gajanan Ghadge, senior inspector of Panvel taluka police, informed that the complaint was lodged by medical officer Dr Sayali Mankar, 33, who inspected Haq's clinic in Kasalkhand village and found that he was an unqualified and unregistered medical practitioner allegedly practising modern medicine by posing as a doctor.He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.Inspector Ghadge said, "We have invoked relevant sections of the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act, 1961, against the accused, which prohibit any person from practising medicine in the state unless their name is registered under the relevant statutory provisions and prescribe criminal penalties and fines for those who illegally practise medicine without valid registration. Under the law, the accused was served a notice under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directing him to appear for inquiry when summoned and during the court proceedings. "
Article Summary: The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal. He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.

Article Title: 'Grabbed hand and attempted to disrobe': Cab driver tries to assault woman passenger near Navi Mumbai airport
Article Text:
Police have registered a case and are searching for the accused driver (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver who took the vehicle to a deserted road near Navi Mumbai airport late on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport, police said. The accused allegedly stopped the cab on the pretext of drinking water before moving to the rear seat beside the woman, police said.According to the police, the woman was travelling to Panvel after a friend booked a cab for her following the party."The driver stopped the vehicle on the deserted service road, stepped out briefly, and then re-entered the car, sitting on the rear seat next to the woman. He allegedly grabbed her hand and attempted to disrobe her," said an official of the Navi Mumbai Police.The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.After the incident, the woman contacted her family and went to Panvel Police Station to lodge a complaint.Since the alleged incident took place within the jurisdiction of Navi Mumbai airport police station, Panvel police escorted her to the appropriate police station.Based on her complaint, Navi Mumbai Airport Police registered a case against the accused, identified as Mohammad Afzal Shaikh, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police have launched a search for Shaikh and are using technical intelligence to trace his whereabouts.Further investigation is underway.(With ANI inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver. The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport. The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.

Article Title: PM classmate’s battle for land continues despite BJP MLA's exit, no possession yet
Article Text:
Asgar Ali Vora met the PM on Sept 8 and sought his intervention in the land disp­u­te





BHAYANDAR: Asgar Ali Vora, a schoolmate of Prime Minister Narendra Modi , continues to struggle to regain possession of his land after MLA Narendra Mehta’s company announced that it had relinquished the property. However, another developer is allegedly continuing to retain possession of the land.Vora, 81, had purchased around 2,810 sq m of land at Navghar in Bhayandar East in 1989. He has alleged that Swayam Builders and Mehta’s Seven Eleven Constructions took possession of the property in 2011. After pursuing the matter for nearly 15 years, Vora met PM Modi on Sep 8 and complained against Mehta.Following the meeting, Mehta relinquished possession of the land, while the municipal corporation also cancelled the construction permission granted to him.However, the land has allegedly not been handed back to its original owner. Instead, developers Mukesh Parekh and Mervyn Fernandes are allegedly continuing to retain possession of the property. Following a complaint by Shiv Sena, Navghar police have registered a non-cognisable offence against Seven Eleven Constructions, Parekh and Fernandes.
Article Summary: Asgar Ali Vora, 81, had purchased around 2,810 sq m of land at Navghar in Bhayandar East in 1989. He has alleged that Swayam Builders and Mehta’s Seven Eleven Constructions took possession of the property in 2011. After pursuing the matter for nearly 15 years, Vora met PM Modi on Sep 8 and complained.

Article Title: Maharashtra TET paper leak: 2 key accused arrested; 168 buyers on radar
Article Text:
Two key accused in TET paper leak case arrested

How the leak occured





BHIWANDI: Two key accused allegedly linked to 168 prospective buyers of the leaked Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) question paper have been arrested, nearly two months after police busted the racket, with the SIT now probing the wider network and possible transactions.The two — Pune-based govt employee Prakash Misal and Bihar native Ashok Shaw, who was staying in Delhi — were among the remaining prominent accused identified during the probe. Police said Misal was in touch with around 50 people who had shown interest in buying the paper, while Shaw allegedly maintained a list of 118 prospective buyers. The list was recovered from his Delhi residence.Shaw was arrested in Patna, Bihar, while Misal was arrested near Bhiwandi Naka on Sunday after police learnt he was planning to surrender before a court. Both were produced before the Bhiwandi court and remanded in police custody till Sept 23.The SIT has so far verified 18 of the 118 names on Shaw's list and found they were preparing to appear for the TET examination. Verification of the remaining 100 is underway.Police suspect Shaw was directly linked to Solapur-based coaching-class operator Prakash Pawar, who has already been arrested, and was also in contact with alleged mastermind Bijendra Gupta.Investigators are questioning Misal to determine the price at which he allegedly planned to sell the paper and whether any sale took place. Earlier, accused Kapil Dahiya, who had allegedly travelled to Pune to deliver the paper to Misal, told investigators he could not hand it over.Police had busted the racket two days before the scheduled examination, forcing postponement of the TET.DCP Pawan Bansod confirmed the arrests. ACP Sachin Sangle, part of the SIT, told TOI, "Their interrogation will help us establish to whom they intended to sell the paper."Last week, the SIT filed a 3,470-page chargesheet before the Bhiwandi fast-track court against those arrested earlier in the case.With Misal and Shaw's arrests, police said the two remaining prominent accused identified during the investigation have been apprehended. Further arrests will depend on findings from their contacts and financial transactions.
Article Summary: Pune-based govt employee Prakash Misal and Bihar native Ashok Shaw were among the remaining prominent accused identified during the probe. Police said Misal was in touch with around 50 people who had shown interest in buying the paper. Shaw allegedly maintained a list of 118 prospective buyers.

Article Title: Cong neta seeks protection for 'gangrape' survivor, her kin
Article Text:
(Representative image)





THANE: A day after Padgha police registered an FIR against former Kalyan West MLA Narendra Pawar and dismissed policeman Shailesh Patil for allegedly gangraping a 22-year-old married woman at a farmhouse in Bapgaon, Congress group leader in KDMC Kanchan Kulkarni on Friday sought police protection for the survivor and her family.Kulkarni, who accompanied the woman to the police station, claimed the survivor's life was in danger because of the accused's influence. She urged CM Eknath Shinde to intervene and ensure security for her.Meanwhile, Padgha police conducted a spot panchnama at the farmhouse in Bapgaon to collect forensic evidence. Seperate police teams have also been formed to trace Pawar and Patil, who remain absconding. Pawar has denied the charge, calling them false. He has also resigned from all his BJP organisational posts. - Pradeep Gupta
Article Summary: Congress group leader in KDMC Kanchan Kulkarni sought police protection for the survivor and her family. She urged CM Eknath Shinde to intervene and ensure security for her. Padgha police conducted a spot panchnama at the farmhouse in Bapgaon to collect forensic evidence.

Article Title: Boy glued to mobile phone run over by train in Chennai
Article Text:
Chennai





: A 17-year-old boy, standing on a railway track, glued to his mobile phone looking for directions to reach a marriage hall, was run over by a train at Thiruvottriyur railway station on Monday evening.The deceased was identified as Gurucharan of New Washermenpet. Police said the teenager had been taking up catering work part-time and was heading to a marriage hall in Ernavoor for an assignment. While crossing the railway tracks at Thiruvottiyur, Gurucharan was looking at his mobile phone for directions and failed to notice the approaching express train.The train knocked him down, killing him on the spot. On receiving information, the railway police reached the spot and recovered the body. It was sent to a govt hospital for postmortem.Police have registered a case and are investigating.
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Gurucharan of New Washermenpet. Police said the teenager had been taking up catering work part-time and was heading to a marriage hall in Ernavoor for an assignment. While crossing the railway tracks at Thiruvottiyur, he was looking at his mobile phone for directions.

Article Title: Two held for possessing prescription tablets for illegal sale in Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: RS Puram police have arrested two men on charges of possessing prescription tablets for illegal sale. Police seized 159 tablets from the duo, identified as R Sabarisan Vishwa, 23, of Ramesh Nagar near Achanur in Thanjavur and N Thilagar, 23, of Anna Nagar in Thuraiyur.On Sunday, police received a tip-off about drug pill sales near the DB Road in RS Puram. Following this, they waited before a lodge in RS Puram. During late hours of Sunday, Vishwa and Thilagar came out of the lodge. Upon checking them, police found drug pills in their possession.Police conducted a search in the room the two men were staying in and found more tablets, syringes with needles and Rs 60,000 in cash. Police seized the tablets, syringes, cash and their mobile phones.Further inquiries revealed that Vishwa and Thilagar had procured the contraband from Trichy. They used to visit Coimbatore once a month and stay in the lodge. Since visitors were not allowed inside the lodge, they contacted the buyers over the phone and sold the contraband in places near the lodge.Police registered a case under sections of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The duo were remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: RS Puram police have arrested two men on charges of possessing prescription tablets for illegal sale. Police seized 159 tablets from the duo, identified as R Sabarisan Vishwa, 23, and N Thilagar, 23. The duo were remanded in judicial custody.

Article Title: Explosive materials seized from godown near Chinnalapatti; two booked
Article Text:
Explosive materials seized from godown near Chinnalapatti; two booked

Dindigul:





Dindigul district police raided a godown in Chinnalapatti on Monday and recovered 1,189kg of explosive materials hoarded illegally.Following a tip-off regarding the illegal hoarding of explosive substances, a police team headed by Chinnalapatti police inspector Sathya raided an asbestos-roofed godown situated within the JNS Bakery premises along the Munnilaikottai–Aariyanallur road.According to police, the raid revealed that the property belongs to Sellathurai, also known as Savarimuthu, 64, a resident of South Street in Aariyanallur.About a month ago, the facility had been rented out to Vijayakumar , 39, of Madurai.Police discovered that the warehouse was being used to hoard explosive ingredients and semi-finished products to manufacture paper crackers commonly used for funerals, temple festivals and wedding celebrations, without any valid licence or safety permissions.During the search, personnel seized 1,048kg of unwound paper crackers, 100kg of magic sand, 34kg of fuse wire, 5kg of chemical white powder, and 2kg of gunpowder.Acting on a complaint lodged by Jayalakshmi, village administrative officer of Munnilaikottai village, Chinnalapatti police registered a case against Vijayakumar and Sellathurai.Both accused individuals were absconding, and special teams have launched an active manhunt to track them down and place them under arrest.
Article Summary: Dindigul district police raided a godown in Chinnalapatti on Monday and recovered 1,189kg of explosive materials hoarded illegally. The warehouse was being used to manufacture paper crackers commonly used for funerals, temple festivals and wedding celebrations.

Article Title: Tension in Thoothukudi over PMT leader’s arrest over extortion plaint
Article Text:
Tension in Thoothukudi over PMT leader’s arrest over extortion plaint





Thoothukudi: Tension prevailed in Thoothukudi on Tuesday after police arrested Pasumpon Muthuramalinga Thevar Makkal Paadhugappu Iyakkam (PMT) leader K Esakki Raja following a complaint from a jeweller accusing him of demanding money and issuing threats. Police resorted to a lathicharge to disperse his supporters who held a road blockade outside the court protesting his arrest.K Esakki Raja, 46, a resident of Pasumpon Nagar near Third Mile, was picked up from his house by Thoothukudi South police on Tuesday morning and taken to the police station for questioning. Police said a case was registered against him following a complaint from Velavan Jewellers alleging extortion and criminal intimidation.Police said the dispute has its roots in a three-year-old incident involving Esakkiraj, a functionary of the same party. He had purchased jewellery from Velavan Jewellers in 2023 and subsequently approached a private finance firm to pledge it. He was allegedly informed that the ornaments contained a higher proportion of other metals.Police said K Esakki Raja had intervened in the dispute on behalf of Esakkiraj and allegedly held a kangaroo court.Police also alleged that K Esakki Raja had received Rs 4.22 lakh towards the jewellery dispute and that he demanded another Rs 1 crore from the owner.The management approached police through representatives of the traders' association and lodged a complaint with the district superintendent of police. Police said Esakki Raja was booked for alleged extortion and criminal intimidation after his arrest by Thoothukudi South police on Tuesday.As a large number of PMT supporters gathered outside the police station, the main entrance to the station was closed and armed personnel deployed. When police took Esakki Raja to the medical college hospital for examination, his supporters tried to block the police vehicle and raised slogans demanding his release. Raja was taken back to south police station before being produced before judicial magistrate in Thoothukudi. The magistrate subsequently remanded him in judicial custody till Oct 6.Following the court order, PMT supporters blocked Thoothukudi-Palayamkottai road in front of the court, alleging that police had registered a false case against their leader. After talks failed to yield results, police resorted to lathicharge to restore traffic.While PMT functionaries maintained that the case against Esakki Raja was retaliatory, police said it was based on a complaint accusing him of demanding money and threatening the jewellery establishment.
Article Summary: Pasumpon Muthuramalinga Thevar Makkal Paadhugappu Iyakkam (PMT) leader K Esakki Raja arrested. Police said a case was registered against him following a complaint from Velavan Jewellers alleging extortion and criminal intimidation. Police resorted to a lathicharge to disperse his supporters who held a road blockade outside the court protesting his arrest.

Article Title: Palani mutt land case: CB-CID gets custody of accused
Article Text:
file picture

Madurai:





Dindigul CB-CID officials have taken custody of Jeyaprakash, an accused in the case pertaining to fraudulent registration of land belonging to Arulmigu Dhandapani Swamigal Madam in Palani in Dindigul district, for interrogation.CB-CID officials filed an application before the principal district court in Dindigul seeking custody of Jeyaprakash. Article Title: Auto driver arrested for threatening, assaulting cops in Yercaud
Article Text:
Representative image





SALEM: The Yercaud police have arrested an autorickshaw driver on charges of assaulting a special sub-inspector (SSI) and threatening to kill the SSI and a woman police constable.The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. Yuvraj, who was drunk, obstructed vehicles near a Vinayagar statue on Monday. Head constable D Thavamani, who was regulating traffic, intervened. Yuvraj abused her verbally.SSI Aaron Athirubaraj attempted to defuse the situation. “But Yuvraj tore my shirt, struck me on the chest and threatened to kill me and Thavamani,” the SSI said.Police registered a case against Yuvraj under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation. Article Title: ED report: Crime Branch SIT to probe CMRL-Exalogic deals
Article Text:
Thiruvananthapuram

:





The state govt has decided to investigate the CMRL-Exalogic financial transactions based on information shared by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) with the state police chief, home minister Ramesh Chennithala said on Tuesday.It is reliably learnt that the preliminary inquiry will be conducted by a special investigation team of the Crime Branch. Earlier, the ED, which is investigating the CMRL bribe case, had written to state police chief Ravada A Chandrasekhar seeking registration of an FIR under the Prevention of Corruption Act against former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan , his daughter Veena T and son-in-law and former minister Mohamed Riyas, based on “evidence” allegedly gathered during its probe.Ramesh said the probe decision was taken in consultation with chief minister V D Satheesan after the govt received the advocate general’s legal opinion. The advocate general had advised that the report received by the police chief could not be ignored and specifically referred to the Supreme Court’s Vijay Madanlal Choudhary judgment, he said.The apex court had held that information shared by the ED with the jurisdictional police under Section 66(2) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) has to be acted upon in accordance with law.According to the minister, the home department subsequently directed an inquiry into the information furnished by the ED. The advocate general also referred to the Supreme Court’s Lalita Kumari judgment, which laid down the procedure to follow before registering an FIR in certain categories of cases, including corruption cases, he said.The legal position laid down in the judgment was explained in detail in the advocate general’s opinion, based on which the govt decided to proceed with a preliminary inquiry, Ramesh said.Section 66(2) of the PMLA provides for sharing information with the agency concerned for necessary action when material available with the ED indicates a possible violation of another law.
Article Summary: The state govt has decided to investigate the CMRL-Exalogic financial transactions based on information shared by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) with the state police chief. It is reliably learnt that the preliminary inquiry will be conducted by a special investigation team of the Crime Branch. Earlier, the ED had written to state. police chief Ravada A Chandrasekhar seeking registration of an FIR. against former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan.

Article Title: Kerala High Court reserves order on prosecution sanction in SNDP fraud
Article Text:
Kerala High Court

Kochi

:





The Kerala HC on Tuesday reserved its order on the legal question of whether prosecution sanction from the state govt is required under the PC Act in cases related to the alleged microfinance fraud involving office-bearers of the SNDP Yogam.Justice A Badharudeen was considering a 2020 petition filed by M S Anil of Cherthala seeking a vigilance probe into the alleged microfinance fraud. The court had sought the state govt’s view on the issue during the previous hearing and heard the matter in detail on Tuesday.On Tuesday, the state attorney appearing for the state govt submitted that specific instructions from the Backward Classes Development Department were that no prosecution sanction was required, as the accused persons — office-bearers of the SNDP Yogam — would not come under the purview of public servants but would be private parties. He further contended that the loan amount was sanctioned by the Backward Classes Development Corporation to the Yogam as an NGO and not in any other capacity. Hence, no prosecution sanction was required against the accused persons.Meanwhile, the Court noted that the vigilance investigation team had previously submitted that the final reports in cases related to the alleged microfinance fraud had been forwarded to the state govt seeking prosecution sanction under the PC Act.The court also orally asked whether the Vigilance and Backward Classes Development departments had different views on the matter.In reply, the state attorney clarified that the definite stand of the state govt was that no prosecution sanction was required in the cases. Previously, counsel for the petitioner had argued that the accused persons were public servants as defined under Section 2(c)(xii) of the PC Act. After hearing both sides on Tuesday, the court reserved its order.
Article Summary: The Kerala HC on Tuesday reserved its order on the legal question of whether prosecution sanction is required under the PC Act. Justice A Badharudeen was considering a 2020 petition filed by M S Anil of Cherthala seeking a vigilance probe into the alleged microfinance fraud. The court had sought the state govt's view on the issue during the previous hearing.

Infopark Police arrested Arayankavu native Sarath K G, 27, on Tuesday in connection with an alleged cheating case.He was listed as the second accused in an FIR registered in April based on the complaint of a 65-year-old man hailing from Mamanglam.The accused entered into an agreement with the complainant to construct six apartments across three floors on a 4.3-cent plot in Thengode, for a total cost of Rs 70 lakh within one year. The case was registered under BNS Sections 316 (2), 318 (4) and 3 (5) for criminal breach of trust, cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property and joint liability.
